title: Stalled-stream detection, segmentation, and partial-output isolation
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: client connections occasionally close mid-generation (abrupt disconnects, mobile app backgrounding, flaky proxies). Today these cases either leak memory for the duration of token TTLs or immediately discard partial payloads without any signal to callers or downstream tools. We need a unified approach that detects stalled/aborted streams quickly, segments partial generations for safe retention, and exposes a clear, lightweight compatibility path for older SDKs and private deployments with restricted resource budgets.

Goals: 
- Detect truly stalled streams vs transient pauses (network hiccups, client backoff) with <5s median detection time for definite aborts.
- Isolate partial generation outputs into an ephemeral, tenant-scoped quarantine so we can offer resume, inspection for debugging, or safe GC.
- Provide a compatibility shim for legacy SDKs that close sockets aggressively (return 204/empty) so hosts don’t keep partial state forever.
- Ensure solution works in hosted, dedicated, and private (VPC/on-prem) with configurable retention and low per-tenant memory footprint.
technical_notes:
Core concepts:
- Segmented generation: chunk in server-side segments (segment_id + seq) instead of one monolithic partial blob. Allows targeted GC and resumability.
- Quarantine metadata: minimal tombstone with origin client_id, model, route, created_at, last_update, resume_token (opaque).
- Abort heuristics: combine client TCP FIN detection, websocket close events, and a soft heartbeat timeout. Three-tier state machine: ACTIVE -> PENDING-SUSPEND -> QUARANTINED -> GC.
- Resource caps: per-tenant segment count + total bytes quota. On breach, oldest quarantine entries evict FIFO or by quality_score.
- Compatibility shim: if client announces legacy-sdk=true in headers, we shorten PENDING-SUSPEND window and emit a synthetic resume_token in headers of the final chunk so SDKs can treat a short-lived token as checkpoint.
- Observability: events for STALLED_DETECTED, QUARANTINED_CREATED, QUARANTINED_RESUMED, QUARANTINED_GC with route/tenant/model tags and sample traces.

Memory considerations for on-prem: default quarantine retention 30s, configurable down to 5s for constrained environments. Quarantine store uses an LRU with soft evict to disk if on-prem operator configures local persistent cache.

Performance goals: additional latency on commit path <1ms p99; GC background worker should reclaim at least 95% of leaked segments within 60s of GC window on 1k concurrent tenants.
implementation_plan:
1) Design phase (1 sprint): finalize state machine and segment schema; spec header/compat shim; design quota config knobs.
2) Prototype (2 weeks): implement server-side segment writer and lightweight tombstone store (in-memory map keyed by resume_token) behind feature flag.
3) Integration (2 weeks): hook into runtime connection handlers: websocket, http streaming, grpc bidi. Add detection events.
4) Opt-in rollout (2 weeks): enable for 10% of traffic on hosted, select Dedicated clusters, and a staging on-prem build.
5) Observability & QA (1 week): dashboards, alerts, chaos tests (simulate disconnects, flakey proxies).
6) Rollout & config UI: add retention/quota knobs to Console and document default values.

Milestones: design doc -> prototype PR -> feature-flag canary -> 50% rollout -> full rollout.
open_questions: What is the default PENDING-SUSPEND window for hosted customers vs private deployments?
Should we expose resume tokens to customers via API or keep them internal for server-side resumption only?
On on-prem deployments without disk persistence, do we require operator to set an explicit small retention to avoid OOM?
decisions: Use segment-level tombstones (segment_id + seq) rather than whole-output blobs to minimize GC work.
Emit a short opaque resume_token for all quarantined outputs; by default tokens are internal but can be surfaced via an opt-in debug flag.
Legacy SDK compatibility: short-circuit PENDING-SUSPEND to 3s for clients that set legacy-sdk=true header; otherwise default 12s for hosted.
Quarantine eviction default: per-tenant segments capped at 5 MB and 50 segments. Exceeding triggers FIFO eviction unless tenant opt-in to quality-based eviction.

2026-02-25 Ethan Park (SRE): Raised concern about quarantine growth in Dedicated clusters with many low-activity tenants. Proposed default per-tenant cap and a background GC scaler. Adding ENG-412001 as dependency for connection signals.
2026-03-01 Diego Martinez: Prototype PR opened https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1983. Added feature-flag streaming.quarantine.enabled and config knobs for retention/quota.

2026-03-05 QA Team: Manual run of disconnect scenarios passed for hosted canary at 10% traffic. Detected STALLED_DETECTED events and quarantined segments were GC'd per configured thresholds. Minor flake observed when legacy-sdk header present; Diego investigating.
